description: §14.8.9 raw-egress fail-closed — a protected row reaching a compiler-unanalyzable egress (a `_={ … }=` foreign-code block, §23) without reveal fires E-PROTECT-004 (error). The floor cannot prove redaction at an un-analyzable sink, so it fails closed rather than silently ship the protected column.
rationale: §14.8.9 closed-world precondition: an egress path the compiler cannot analyze (`_{}` foreign block, `asIs` value) carrying a protected-origin column SHALL fail closed with E-PROTECT-004 — the confidentiality sibling of the read-site E-PROTECT-001, in the return-boundary direction. I-PROTECT-STRIP-001 co-fires (the SELECT * is tagged). ⚑ The block is written at LEVEL 1 (`_={ … }=`) on purpose. SPEC §23.2 defines the opener as `_` + zero or more `=` + `{`, and W-FOREIGN-001 steers authors AWAY from the level-0 `_{`; until S405 this gate's own predicate matched level 0 ONLY, so it recognized exactly the spelling the compiler discourages and missed every recommended one. This case therefore goes RED against the pre-S405 emitter and is a proof of the level-family fix, not a description of it. The case previously used a manual `new Response(...)`; that shape moved to E-PROTECT-005 (`e-protect-005-pos`) when the `Response` kind was promoted from this source-text lint to a structural emission-time gate.
